timing_updates.body:
Coach baseline met the agreed limits: warm p95 0.46 s, two-concurrent p95 0.42 s and the first request after idle 21.05 s. Cloud Run logs confirm that the idle request started a new instance. These were bounded checks, not a sustained-load test.

[Timing results](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/blob/45b0633/docs/iteration-17/verification/timing/acceptance-summary.json)

Waited until Cloud Run reported zero active and zero idle instances, then sent one coach-baseline request. It returned five valid rankings in 21.05 s, below the 45 s limit. The request and AUTOSCALING startup logs identify the same new instance.

[Timing results](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/blob/45b0633/docs/iteration-17/verification/timing/acceptance-summary.json)

All three agreed coach-baseline limits passed on the current deployment: warm p95 0.46 s, two-concurrent p95 0.42 s and first request after idle 21.05 s. The limits were 5 s, 10 s and 45 s. The startup result is one measured cold request, not a percentile.

[Timing results](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/blob/45b0633/docs/iteration-17/verification/timing/acceptance-summary.json)

legacy_case_updates.body:
Toronto against Boston in 2024–25 returned five rankings with the requested season, teams and weights. Every row had a play type and valid PPP prediction and gap values.

[Executed requests](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/blob/main/docs/iteration-17/verification/legacy-baseline/results.json)

Missing our and k=-1 returned HTTP 422. The unknown season and empty our value returned HTTP 400. Each error included a JSON detail and no rankings.

[Executed requests](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/blob/main/docs/iteration-17/verification/legacy-baseline/results.json)
